html:
SMTO-LLM-0008 — SMTO lost its connection to the model for an unknown reason

GUID: 639b6d4c-b43d-4bff-af73-6a78770c2b19
Slug: llm-transport-error
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't get a complete reply from the model because the connection failed, and the exact reason wasn't recorded. SMTO didn't act on any part of that reply.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and select Check saved model. This quick test shows whether SMTO can reach the model server right now.
  2. If the check fails, make sure the computer or service running the model is switched on, and that your network or VPN connection is working. The connection broke somewhere between SMTO and the model server, so that path is the first thing to confirm.
  3. When the check passes, on the stopped task, select Resume (or Continue task if that is what it shows). SMTO never acted on the failed reply, so continuing is safe and steps the task already finished are kept.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model shows its checks passing, and the task shows new activity without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the time it happened, to the person who manages the model server so they can match it with their logs. Don't delete SMTO's data or turn off its safety checks to get past this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A model request failed with a transport exception that the classifier could not map to a timeout, refusal, reset, DNS, TLS or routing cause, so the exact cause is unknown (llm_transport_error).

What this means

  • SMTO did not obtain a complete model response, and the transport classifier could not identify a narrower category. This is not evidence of a particular DNS, TLS, credential or hardware problem. Diagnosis needs the bounded technical detail and the request phase.

Why this can happen

  • The underlying transport cause is not established by this category.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the occurrence’s exception type, request phase and provider status if present. Ask the provider operator to correlate that time with service and network logs, without sharing prompts or response bodies.

How to fix it

  • Read provider_diagnostic in the error details (stream_failure_stage, http_status, llm_base_url) and compare the request time with the provider's and any proxy's logs. Test the endpoint with Check saved model, repair the component that dropped the request, then resume; this category is not evidence of a DNS, TLS or credential fault.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and ask the provider operator to compare the request time and phase with service logs. Choose a repair only after the failing component is identified.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A controlled request to the same endpoint returns a complete response; recurring failures retain a more specific diagnostic.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Typed transport exception (or exact legacy standard reason where supported); no tool outcome is inferred from connection state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
